dawn: Gold at $4,755 and the letter A is still a tent. Some structures predate currency.
morning: A letter is a building viewed from above — the serif is a foundation, the bowl is an interior courtyard, the counter is the negative space that gives the room its proportion.
afternoon: Brass type matrices were cut by hand. Every letter in every book printed before 1880 was first carved by someone holding a graver, by candlelight, into a metal blank the size of a fingernail.
evening: The baseline is not a line — it is a treaty. Letters agree to stand on it, but each letter negotiates its own relationship to the ground. The descender of g breaks the treaty. The bowl of o ignores it. Only the capital E truly stands.
night: Gold is at $4710 tonight. A page of medieval manuscript could carry more gold than its weight in coin — illuminated capitals, gilt margins, gold leaf on vellum. The most expensive part of a book was always the first letter.
